title: Workday’s $51 billion takeover talks could reset the software trade

content_html:
For much of 2026, software investors have been grappling with a terrifying question: What if artificial intelligence makes many of the apps that firms have spent decades buying considerably less valuable?

If Workday (WDAY) is acquired, that argument could lead Wall Street to reconsider how far it has gone.

Shares of Workday jumped about 18% after it emerged that Silver Lake, a technology-focused private-equity group, was considering an acquisition of the human-resources and financial-management software company.

The development helped raise Workday's market capitalization to more than $51 billion. But talks could still break down, and no deal has been announced.

The valuation is way bigger than Workday.

Software stocks have spent much of the year under pressure from worries that generative AI and autonomous agents will allow companies to build applications more cheaply, automate jobs previously performed by enterprise software, and ultimately lower what businesses are willing to pay for traditional software subscriptions.

But the real business of Workday doesn't look like one that's being rapidly displaced.

The company generated$9.55 billion of revenue in fiscal 2026, up 13.1%, while subscription revenue increased 14.5% to $8.83 billion. In the first quarter of fiscal 2027, revenue climbed another 13.5% to $2.54 billion, with subscription revenue rising 14.3%.

That makes the prospective Silver Lake interest even more interesting.

Private equity may be eyeing the same software businesses that public investors have been discounting out of concern of AI disruption and finding resilient recurring revenue, deeply ingrained customers, and assets that have just gotten cheaper.

Workday's numbers complicate the AI disruption story

AI is a genuine threat to segments of the software business.

If firms are able to employ AI agents to write code, automate operations, and quickly build internal applications, some traditional software solutions could be under pressure on pricing or see reduced demand.

But seeing every business software company as similarly vulnerable misses a fundamental distinction.

Workday lies at the intersection of human resources, payroll-related operations, and corporate finance systems that can hold years of company data, connectors, permissions, and business rules.

Taking one away can be hugely disruptive.

That introduces switching costs that a new AI application doesn't automatically eliminate.

That stickiness shows up in Workday's financial outcomes. Subscription revenue grew 14.5% in fiscal 2026 and continued to rise at 14.3% in the first quarter of fiscal 2027.

content_html_zh:
在 2026 年的大部分时间里，软件投资者一直在努力解决一个可怕的问题：如果人工智能使企业花费数十年时间购买的许多应用程序的价值大大降低怎么办？

如果 Workday (WDAY) 被收购，这一论点可能会导致华尔街重新考虑它已经走了多远。

在专注于技术的私募股权集团 Silver Lake 正在考虑收购这家人力资源和财务管理软件公司后，Workday 的股价上涨了约 18%。

这一发展帮助 Workday 的市值增至超过 510 亿美元。 但谈判仍可能破裂，目前尚未宣布任何协议。

估值比Workday大得多。

今年的大部分时间里，软件股都承受着压力，因为人们担心生成式人工智能和自主代理将使公司能够更便宜地构建应用程序，使以前由企业软件执行的工作实现自动化，并最终降低企业愿意为传统软件订阅支付的费用。

但 Workday 的真正业务看起来并没有被迅速取代。

该公司在 2026 财年实现收入 95.5 亿美元，增长 13.1%，订阅收入增长 14.5%，达到 88.3 亿美元。 2027 财年第一季度，收入再增长 13.5% 至 25.4 亿美元，其中订阅收入增长 14.3%。

这使得银湖的潜在兴趣变得更加有趣。

私募股权公司可能会关注公共投资者出于对人工智能颠覆的担忧而一直打折的软件业务，并寻找有弹性的经常性收入、根深蒂固的客户以及刚刚变得更便宜的资产。

Workday 的数据让人工智能颠覆的故事变得更加复杂

人工智能对软件业务的各个领域构成了真正的威胁。

如果公司能够使用人工智能代理来编写代码、自动化操作并快速构建内部应用程序，一些传统的软件解决方案可能会面临定价压力或需求减少。

但如果认为每家商业软件公司都同样容易受到攻击，那么就忽略了一个根本区别。

Workday 位于人力资源、薪资相关操作和企业财务系统的交叉点，可以保存多年的公司数据、连接器、权限和业务规则。

拿走一个可能会造成巨大的破坏。

这就带来了新的人工智能应用程序无法自动消除的转换成本。

这种粘性体现在 Workday 的财务业绩中。 2026 财年订阅收入增长 14.5%，2027 财年第一季度继续增长 14.3%。
